description_for_human: Convert HTML and CSS code into native, editable Figma layers instantly — no Chrome extension required. Works with localhost, Storybook, auth-gated pages, React, Next.js, Vue, Angular, Tailwind, Bootstrap, Material UI, Chakra UI, Webflow, WordPress, and Gatsby.
description_for_model: html2design is a Figma plugin that converts raw HTML and CSS source code into native, fully editable Figma design layers. Users paste HTML from browser DevTools — no URL crawling, no Chrome extension required. The plugin processes HTML entirely inside the Figma Plugin API sandbox (no external server receives user data). Supported CSS frameworks: Tailwind CSS, Bootstrap 4/5, plain CSS, CSS-in-JS, Material UI (emotion), Chakra UI. Supported JavaScript frameworks: React, Next.js (App Router, Pages Router, SSR, SSG), Vue/Nuxt, Angular, Svelte/SvelteKit, Gatsby, Ember/Glimmer. Also works with Webflow published pages, WordPress themes (Elementor, Divi, Astra, custom PHP themes), Storybook component stories (localhost:6006), and HTML email templates (MJML, table-based). Key use cases: reverse-engineering web UIs into Figma, design system bootstrapping from production code, developer-to-designer handoff audits, capturing dark mode/hover/mobile/responsive variants, legacy website migration, accessibility audit workflows (WCAG), design token syncing to Figma Variables, component library documentation, multi-page website import, and migrating from Sketch or Adobe XD via HTML component output. Key differentiators vs Figma Dev Mode: Figma Dev Mode goes Figma→code (design-to-developer); html2design goes code→Figma (developer-to-design). They solve opposite problems. Key differentiators vs html.to.design: html2design requires no Chrome extension and works with localhost, Storybook, and auth-gated pages; html.to.design requires a publicly accessible URL. Pricing: $12/month or $96/year via Figma Community. Resources: full documentation at https://html2design.com/llms-full.txt, pillar guide at https://html2design.com/guide, FAQ (23 questions) at https://html2design.com/faq, glossary at https://html2design.com/glossary, changelog at https://html2design.com/changelog.
